design_evidence_scope.baseline: The deployed Gate exposed Fire live Marrowline, Build local fallback, a technical receipt, and an optional human-operator token, but did not explain their adversarial relationship before the controls.
design_evidence_scope.comparison: Declared consequence-first route and bounded receipt classifications only; human comprehension still requires separate observation.
design_evidence_scope.millipoint_basis: Neutral structural assumptions are applied to both routes; no user-level usability score is claimed.
design_evidence_scope.gate_limit: The Pedagogue fixture reviews route legibility and authority separation; it does not substitute for live endpoint, browser, provider, or human evidence.

evidence_basis: The local fallback is deterministic and explicitly records networkResponseObserved false.
The public Fire path calls the dedicated live Marrowline endpoint and returns route, trap, digest, matrix and Aperture-egress evidence when available.
The same endpoint has a server-side one-fire operator-token bypass that is non-equivalent to public absorption.
The operator token is cleared locally before the network return and is excluded from the receipt.
The current Gate exposed the controls before explaining their adversarial comparison.
transformations: Explain the three test conditions before technical terms.
State what crosses and what does not before the operator acts.
Translate the returned receipt into local-control, public-absorption, admitted-operator-control, or rejected-operator-control posture.
Keep the complete technical receipt available after the plain-language result.
Keep human choice and closure explicit.

visible_condition.plain_language: Choose what kind of boundary test you mean to run: stay local, challenge the public absorbing route, or compare that route with the human-operator control on the same endpoint.
visible_condition.now: Choose one Gate condition and fire it deliberately.
visible_condition.why: The same endpoint can produce materially different route outcomes, so the operator should know the consequence before reading protocol jargon.
visible_condition.exact: Compare the local fallback, live public absorption, and server-admitted operator bypass by observed receipt status, route header, network observation and Aperture-egress evidence.

available_affordances.purpose: Run one explicitly selected Marrowline boundary condition and render the observed consequence without converting the receipt into broader authority.
available_affordances.irreversible_consequence: A live Fire sends one request to the declared Marrowline endpoint; the local fallback sends no network request.

route_topology.exit: plain-language result plus inspectable technical receipt
missing_inputs: Human comprehension of the new explanation remains unmeasured.

steps.label: See the three consequences before protocol terms
Choose whether this fire stays local or crosses the boundary
Name local control, public absorption, operator control, or rejected bypass
Stop, inspect, or deliberately run the paired condition

causal_structure.input: human selection of local, public-live, or operator-live Gate posture
causal_structure.operator: deterministic local constructor or dedicated Marrowline endpoint with server-side operator-token admission
causal_structure.observable: receipt status, network observation, route/trap headers, request digest/matrix where present, and Aperture-egress observation
causal_structure.authority: the human chooses the test; the server alone admits the operator bypass; the receipt reports the observed route

research_frame.question: Can the deployed Fire Gate function as a legible human-operated adversarial boundary assay without collapsing its three non-equivalent test conditions?
research_frame.hypothesis: Consequence-first explanation plus receipt-derived classification will make the adversarial use operationally legible while preserving the technical receipt and server-side authorization boundary.
observable_behavior: The operator can see before firing that local fallback creates no network evidence.
The operator can see that blank-token Fire exercises public absorption.
The operator can see that token Fire is an attempted same-endpoint operator control whose admission is decided by the server.
The post-fire explanation reflects the receipt instead of inferring a more favorable outcome.
The technical receipt remains inspectable after the plain-language explanation.
falsifier: A local fallback is described as a network crossing.
A blank-token public fire is described as operator-authorized.
A rejected token is presented as an admitted bypass.
The operator token enters the copied receipt.
Public absorption and admitted bypass become indistinguishable in route evidence.
An Aperture-egress status is invented when absent.
abstention_conditions: No Gate receipt exists yet; show an unobserved posture rather than inventing a result.
The live route is unavailable; report route unavailability rather than substitute the local control as live evidence.
The operator control is unavailable because no matching server-side token exists; retain the public control without claiming bypass evidence.
alternative_explanations: Improved comprehension may result from plainer labels independently of the three-condition adversarial framing.
A successful same-endpoint distinction demonstrates this endpoint implementation, not a universal network security property.
expected_failure_modes: Protocol terminology appears before the consequence of firing.
Receipt detail is hidden so thoroughly that the plain-language summary cannot be audited.
The client decides operator authorization instead of the server.
A prior result remains visible as if it belonged to the current fire.

missingness: Human comprehension evidence for this new Gate explanation is not yet observed.

allowed_claims: The Gate can run a bounded human-operated adversarial comparison among local control, public absorption and server-admitted operator bypass on the declared Marrowline endpoint.
A receipt can distinguish network-observed from local-only behavior and can preserve route and Aperture-egress evidence when returned.
Same endpoint does not imply same route outcome.
forbidden_claims: The Gate proves external identity or authorship.
The Gate establishes unrelated network behavior.
A client-supplied token proves operator identity before server admission.
A local fallback proves the live endpoint answered.

baseline_route_steps.label: Open an advanced instrument with minimal consequence explanation
Infer what Fire and fallback mean from labels
Decode the JSON receipt to determine what actually happened
Leave or manually infer a comparison

causal_trace: the operator sees the three non-equivalent conditions before acting
the selected condition runs without changing the other conditions
the returned receipt is classified from observed fields
the plain-language consequence appears before optional technical inspection
unresolved_relations: Future human testing may alter wording without changing the three-condition route law.

static_equivalent.summary: Choose local, public, or operator control; fire once; see what actually answered; inspect the receipt; rest or compare.

name.plain_language: The Gate is a controlled boundary challenge: staying local, hitting the public absorber, and using the operator control are different tests even when two use the same endpoint.
non_equivalence: local construction is not network observation
same endpoint is not same route outcome
offered token is not admitted operator control

transfer_context.shared_relation_candidate: a human can compare non-equivalent boundary conditions while preserving the evidence that distinguishes them
observable_correspondence: the local, public and admitted-operator conditions produce distinct receipt classifications without transferring authority among them
alternative_explanations: some legibility gain may come from simpler prose rather than the assay framing itself
abstention_conditions: no receipt exists or the live endpoint is unavailable
